{{nihongo|'''Tenjin Shrine'''|天神神社 (岐阜市柳津町)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Owari Province]].

It is also called Yanaizu Tenjin Shrine.

It is Anahobe Shrine of Haguri District, {{ill|Owari Province|Q514506|qid=Q514506}}, in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki}} (there is also a theory that Anahobe Shrine is {{ill|Kamo Shrine (Ichinomiya)|Q11634949|qid=Q11634949|lt=Kamo Shrine}} in Ichinomiya, Aichi).

The current Tenjin Shrine is a merged shrine of Anahobe Shrine, Kita-Tenjin Shrine, and Naka-Tenjin Shrine.

=== Outline ===
*The founding time of Anahobe Shrine is unclear, but one account says it was founded in the 6th century as the guardian shrine of Taishi-dera (present {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kōtaku-ji}}), founded by {{ill|Prince Shōtoku|ar|شوتوكو تايشي|azb|شوتوکو تایشی|be|Сётоку Тайсі|ca|Shotoku Taishi|cs|Princ Šótoku|de|Shōtoku|es|Shōtoku|fa|شاهزاده شوتوکو تایشی|fi|Shōtoku (prinssi)|fr|Shōtoku (prince du Japon)|hr|Shōtoku|hu|Sótoku japán régensherceg|id|Pangeran Shōtoku|it|Umayado|ja|聖徳太子|jv|Pangéran Shōtoku|ka|შოტოკუ|ko|쇼토쿠 태자|la|Shotoku Taishi|nl|Shotoku Taishi|no|Shotoku|pl|Shōtoku (książę)|pt|Shōtoku Taishi|ro|Shōtoku|ru|Сётоку (принц)|sh|Princ Shōtoku|sq|Shotoku Taishi|sr|Принц Шотоку|sv|Prins Shōtoku|th|เจ้าชายโชโตกุ|tr|Prens Shōtoku|uk|Принц Сьотоку|vi|Thánh Đức Thái tử|zh|聖德太子|zh_classical|聖德太子|zh_min_nan|Sèng-tek Thài-chú|qid=Q263972}}. The enshrined deity was {{ill|Ame no Hohi|qid=Q10940685|lt=Ame-no-Hohi-no-Mikoto}}. The location is said to have been about 500 m south of the current Tenjin Shrine. In the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}} it was called “Akata Tenjin” and was the guardian shrine of Kōtaku-ji, but became independent through {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|Q1970535|qid=Q1970535}} in the {{ill|Meiji era|lt=Meiji period|qid=Q3125096}}.
*Kita-Tenjin Shrine was founded in {{ill|1557|Q6595|qid=Q6595}} ({{ill|Kōji (Muromachi period)|Q1143910|qid=Q1143910|lt=Kōji}} 3) by descendants of Minamoto no Yorizane (or Minamoto no Yorisada), enshrining an image of Sugawara no Michizane made by him; its deity was {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ar|سوغاوارا نو ميتشيزانه|br|Sugawara no Michizane|ckb|سوگاوارا نۆ میچیزانێ|de|Sugawara no Michizane|es|Sugawara no Michizane|fa|سوگاوارا نو میچی‌زانه|fi|Sugawara no Michizane|fr|Sugawara no Michizane|id|Sugawara no Michizane|it|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|菅原道真|kk|Сугавара но Митидзане|ko|스가와라노 미치자네|la|Sugawara no Michizane|ms|Sugawara no Michizane|nl|Sugawara no Michizane|nn|Sugawara no Michizane|pl|Michizane Sugawara|pt|Sugawara no Michizane|ru|Сугавара-но Митидзанэ|sh|Sugawara no Michizane|sv|Sugawara no Michizane|th|สึกาวาระ โนะ มิจิซาเนะ|tr|Sugawara no Michizane|uk|Суґавара но Мітідзане|zh|菅原道真|zh_classical|菅原道真|zh_min_nan|Sugawara no Mitizane|qid=Q382005}}. Naka-Tenjin Shrine has an unknown foundation date.
*In {{ill|1945|Q5240|qid=Q5240}} (Shōwa 20), Anahobe Shrine and Naka-Tenjin Shrine were merged into Kita-Tenjin Shrine, and in {{ill|1954|Q18581|qid=Q18581}} (Shōwa 29) it was renamed Tenjin Shrine. On August 17, {{ill|1965|Q2650|qid=Q2650}} (Shōwa 40), it was designated by the Gifu Prefecture Association of Shinto Shrines as a prefectural shinto association chief-visit designated shrine ({{ill|Kinpei-sha|Q119929592|qid=Q119929592}}), designation No. Kin-63{{sfn|Kimura|1997|p=91}}{{sfn|Gifu Prefecture Association of Shinto Shrines|2017|p=379}}.
